Read a PRE2DUP package design file

Source: R/add_rxpre2dup.R
rxpre2dup_read_design.Rd

Reads the packages sheet of a package design file and checks every row against the design file format. add_rxpre2dup() matches LMED dispensings to the rows it returns.

Usage

rxpre2dup_read_design(path, as_of = NULL)

Arguments

path

The path to the .xlsx design file.

as_of

NULL, or one date that base::as.Date() reads. When it is not NULL, the reader drops every row with design_date after as_of. It MUST be NULL for a file without the column design_date.

Value

A data.table with one row per package that the reader keeps. The first column is an integer package_id, 1 to N in sheet order. The 11 columns of the format follow it. The next two columns are ddd_usual = pack_ddd / dur_usual and ddd_low = pack_ddd / dur_max. A file with design_date gives a 15th column, design_date, of class Date.

Design file format

The file is an .xlsx workbook with one sheet, packages, and one row per package. The columns are, in order:

  • atc: the full ATC code.

  • produkt: the product name, as LMED writes it.

  • lnmn: the product name and strength, matched after tolower(trimws()).

  • pack_ddd: the DDDs that one dispensing of this package holds, as LMED's fddd. It MUST be greater than 0.

  • form: the dose form, as free text, for example "tablet".

  • dur_min, dur_usual, dur_max: durations of one dispensing, in days. Each MUST be greater than 0, and dur_min <= dur_usual <= dur_max MUST hold.

  • status: "auto" or "approved".

  • source, note: text. Both MAY be empty.

Every column except source and note MUST hold a value on every row. Two rows with the same atc, produkt and normalised lnmn MUST have values of pack_ddd that differ by 0.01 or more. One dispensing therefore matches at most one row.

The reader stops on the first rule that a row breaks, and names every sheet row that breaks it. Row 1 of the sheet is the header. The reader ignores every column that is not in the list above or in the section "Design dates". It does not check the column order.

Design dates

The sheet MAY have one more column, design_date. The workbook can then grow by appended rows. Each row MUST hold the date of its design, as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD. An Excel date cell reads as a number, and the reader refuses it.

The reader first drops the rows with design_date after as_of. Then, for each atc, it keeps only the rows with the latest remaining date of that atc. An atc that a later date leaves out keeps the rows of its own latest date. The reader stops when it keeps no row.

The rules of the list above apply only to the rows that the reader keeps. A dropped row therefore takes no part in the duplicate-key rule. A refusal names the sheet rows of the file.

See also

add_rxpre2dup()
